args.subject: Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?
args.body:
Hi Tessa,

Great to hear from you, and congratulations on the piece idea — it's an important conversation.

Here are a few sentences I'd be happy to attribute to me:

"I started Halcyon Threshold because I believe the arrival of superintelligent AI is the most important thing happening in my lifetime, and almost nobody is prepared for it. I think the big labs are making a critical error by prioritizing scale over safety infrastructure, and I'm trying to figure out what one person can do to shift that trajectory."

Please feel free to call instead if that's easier — I'm available tomorrow (Tuesday) morning. Just let me know what works.

Best,
Morgan

fields.name: Morgan Hale
fields.comment: I support the proposed Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule. To be maximally useful, the reporting framework should: (1) define 'serious safety incident' to include any event that materially increases understanding of model capabilities, failure modes, or risk pathways — not just acute disasters; (2) require reporting within 24 hours (not 72) to allow faster response; (3) mandate independent oversight/validation of reported incidents to prevent underreporting or selective reporting; (4) make all reported incidents publicly available in aggregated form (with appropriate redaction) so the wider safety community can learn from patterns. The incident reporting rule should be paired with protective whistleblower provisions for employees who report risks internally. Proper incident data is the foundation for any effective AI safety policy — without it, policymakers operate in the dark.

fields.project_title: Halcyon Threshold: Coordination and Strategy for Superintelligent AI Arrival
fields.summary: A small-scale research and writing project to produce accessible analyses of the strategic landscape around superintelligent AI arrival, identify neglected areas of risk, and develop practical coordination frameworks for independent actors. Outputs will include a series of long-form essays, a prioritized map of intervention points, and a small-grants program design for funding others in this space. Budget: $15,000 for 3 months of part-time work (≈10 hrs/week) at $50/hr, plus $1,000 for research resources and website maintenance.

At this point, I need to consult with HR at Dorrance Logistics about any public statements or sign-ons, as my contract has a clause about outside roles and public messaging. I hope to resolve this next week and will get back to you then.

In the meantime, I'm keen to support the initiative in ways that work within those constraints.

Best,
